disposition_mapping.rationale: Document assembly is pure retrieval with no judgment content; the council converged (maximalist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, pragmatist) that it belongs inside the same automated pass as matching rather than as a standalone human-actored step. Per accounting_standards/finance_domain's non-negotiable (KB-09), the assembled document set must survive as an archived, retrievable evidentiary artifact, and per emerging_economy/agentic_architect's concession, analyst-mediated capture remains a designed-for path where automated retrieval cannot complete.

Quantity matching is deterministic line comparison and is absorbed into the single automated matching pass, but TWM-R-01 and TWM-R-03 are honored because quantity variance detail survives as a separately labelled, individually inspectable output (a point accounting_standards, finance_domain, hitl_designer and the converted agentic_architect/maximalist all required) and GRN data remains a directly consumed input.

Price and terms matching is the same class of mechanical comparison as quantity matching and is merged for the same reason. TWM-R-02/R-04 are satisfied: price and terms variance detail survives as a distinct output and purchase order data remains a directly consumed input, preserving the KB-09 cost-evidence basis (price net of discounts/rebates) that the council treated as non-negotiable.

Against maximalist's and agentic_architect's round-1 position, the council majority (finance_domain, hitl_designer, accounting_standards, pragmatist, and agentic_architect's own round-2 concession) held that tolerance evaluation must remain a structurally distinct step with a named, versioned policy artifact, even though its application is now automated. Folding it invisibly into the matching pass would bury the one object (which policy, whose authority, as of when) auditors and KB-06's policy-consistency principle require to be independently visible. TWM-R-05/R-06 are satisfied: the function survives and still consumes the tolerance policy, now explicitly versioned and governed.

This is the council's clearest near-consensus point: pragmatist, hitl_designer, finance_domain, emerging_economy and accounting_standards all rejected maximalist's autonomous-resolution proposal, and maximalist itself conceded in round 2. KB-05's error-correction principle and KB-09's cost-evidence principle require an accountable human to own every accept/correct/reject decision; a confidence-scored pattern match is not a decision basis. The function is restructured only to add agent-assisted packet assembly, precedent surfacing and an explicit exception-category taxonomy (finance_domain's four categories, adopted by hitl_designer and agentic_architect) — the decision and its evidence remain fully human. TWM-R-10 is satisfied as a genuine, unweakened human function.

The council converged (finance_domain, agentic_architect, hitl_designer, pragmatist, with maximalist arriving independently) that uniform supervisor review of every clean invoice is ceremonial, not control, while the baseline's own text already distinguishes tolerance releases from exception/override releases requiring explicit approval. That distinction is made structural: TGT-04 auto-releases clean/in-tolerance matches under a bounded, reversible void-before-posting window; TGT-05 preserves an explicit, evidenced AP supervisor approval, with a named backup approver, for every exception-resolved or override case. TWM-R-07 survives via both paths; TWM-R-08 holds because TGT-05 consumes TGT-03's resolved-match output before approving; TWM-R-09 holds because TGT-05's supervisor is a distinct actor and distinct system identity from both TGT-03's resolver and TGT-04's automated release engine, addressing agentic_architect's and hitl_designer's point that separation must hold at the credential level, not only the org chart.

Unconstrained by design, so the council had latitude; it converged on moving from a periodic batch report to continuous, append-only logging (maximalist, agentic_architect, finance_domain, accounting_standards) while holding, against a pure 'exception-alert consumer' framing, that a periodic independent human sampling review of the auto-released population must survive (hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards) performed by a reviewer organisationally independent of whoever operates the matching, tolerance-classification and release-automation functions (pragmatist's and accounting_standards' independence concern), with any tolerance recalibration arising from exception-category telemetry routed through TGT-02's human-governed change control rather than automatic adjustment (finance_domain's loop, with agentic_architect's and finance_domain's own guardrail against metrics-driven loosening).

steps.actor: Automated matching engine/agent (system identity: match-execution), with AP analyst oversight of assembly failures and manual-capture fallback
steps.description: The invoice, purchase order and goods receipt note are retrieved (via automated ERP integration where available, or analyst-mediated capture logged identically where system-to-system retrieval is not possible) and compared line by line for quantity and price/terms variance in a single automated pass. Quantity variance detail and price and terms variance detail are produced and retained as separately labelled, individually inspectable outputs, together with an archived copy of the assembled match document set that preserves the invoice-PO-GRN evidence chain underlying cost determination. Where required inputs cannot be assembled (missing PO, unposted GRN, incomplete receipt, unresolved UOM mismatch), the case is routed to a human exception queue; the engine never defaults to a pass on missing or ambiguous data.
steps.name: Automated match assembly and execution
outputs: Assembled match document set (archived evidentiary artifact)

steps.actor: Automated tolerance-classification engine (system identity: tolerance-classification), with named AP control owner accountable for the policy
steps.description: Quantity and price/terms variances are evaluated against a named, versioned, human-governed tolerance policy to classify the match as clean, within tolerance, or an exception requiring investigation. Kept as a distinct step and artifact from TGT-01 so that the policy in force, its version and its owner remain independently auditable rather than embedded as an undocumented parameter inside the matching engine. The classification engine consumes the policy but has no write path to it; threshold changes go through a separate, human-governed change-control process owned by a named AP control owner.
steps.name: Tolerance classification under governed policy

steps.actor: AP analyst (agent-assisted triage; decision and accountability remain human)
steps.description: Matches classified as exceptions are investigated against source documents and vendor correspondence. A triage agent may assemble the exception packet, categorise it (e.g. receiving-timing shortfall, price discrepancy, missing/unposted GRN, duplicate or unauthorised invoice) and propose a disposition with precedent, but the accept/correct/reject decision and its written evidentiary basis remain owned by a named human AP analyst in every case, regardless of materiality or pattern familiarity. No exception is auto-resolved.
steps.name: Agent-assisted exception investigation and human resolution
outputs: Exception resolution evidence, including exception category

steps.actor: Automated release engine (system identity: release-automated, distinct from match-execution and tolerance-classification identities)
steps.description: Matches classified as clean or within tolerance, with no exception resolution outstanding, are released for posting and payment processing by an automated release engine operating under a pre-authorised, versioned release policy. Every auto-release is logged and held in a bounded, reversible void-before-posting window, and is subject to periodic independent human sampling review (TGT-06), before it reaches payment processing.
steps.name: Automated release — clean and in-tolerance matches

steps.actor: AP supervisor (with named backup approver; distinct from TGT-03 resolver and from TGT-04's automated identity)
steps.description: Every exception-resolved match and any release outside standard tolerance is routed to an AP supervisor for explicit, evidenced approval before release. The approving supervisor is a distinct individual from whoever performed the exception resolution and operates under a distinct system identity from the automated release path in TGT-04. A named backup approver is designated so a single-supervisor site or shift does not create a bottleneck or a pressure to bypass the gate.
steps.name: Supervisory release approval — exceptions and overrides

steps.actor: AP accountant / control owner (independent of match-execution, tolerance-classification and release-automation operators)
steps.description: Match outcomes, tolerance overrides, exception resolutions and auto-releases are logged in real time to an append-only control record. An AP accountant/control owner, organisationally independent of whoever operates the matching engine, the tolerance-classification engine and the automated release path, performs periodic sampling review of the auto-released clean/in-tolerance population and produces match-rate and override reporting on a defined cadence, achievable with lightweight tooling where premium platforms are unavailable. Exception-category data from TGT-03 feeds a periodic tolerance-policy recalibration review, but any resulting threshold change must pass through the named-owner change-control process in TGT-02, never an automatic adjustment driven by match-rate pressure.
steps.name: Continuous match control monitoring, sampling review and tolerance governance
outputs: Tolerance recalibration recommendation (subject to governed change control)
